about: The children's page's wording of each question, written by Claude Opus from the 1903 and checked wordings and the BSB; written by scripts/question_children_wording.py.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Who made you?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: God

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Where is God?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Everywhere
wrong: Only in people who love him

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What does the ninth commandment teach us?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: To tell the truth
wrong: Not to take things that aren't ours
Not to want what other people have
To rest on God's special day

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: How do the Ten Commandments help us?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: They show us when we do wrong, and lead us to Jesus to save us
wrong: They make us good enough for heaven all by ourselves
They show us that we don't need Jesus at all
They tell us the day the world will end
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: Romans 3:20 says the law 'merely brings awareness of sin', and Galatians 3:24 says it leads us to Christ. 'Show us what is right' is not what these verses say. The answer now follows the verses more closely.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What is prayer?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Telling God what we need, in Jesus' name, and thanking Him
wrong: Earning God's love by saying nice words
Telling God what He has to do for us
Something only grown-ups are allowed to do
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The answer was a catechism wording ('things He has promised to give'). The verses say to bring our requests to God with thanks (Philippians 4:6) and to ask the Father in Jesus' name (John 16:23-24). Also, the wrong choice about repeating words leans on Matthew 6:7, which is not in these verses, so it was swapped out.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What did Jesus give us to teach us how to pray?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: The Lord's Prayer
wrong: The story of David and Goliath

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: In the Lord's Prayer, what do we ask God to give us this day?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Our daily bread
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The number 'six' comes from one way the catechism counts the requests. The verses do not count them. Some people count 'lead us not into temptation' and 'deliver us from the evil one' as two requests, which makes seven. The new question has one clear answer from Matthew 6:11.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Can you see God?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: No, but he always sees me
wrong: No, and he only sees me when I pray
Yes, when I look at the sky

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: In the Lord's Prayer we say, "Your kingdom come." What are we asking for?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: That God will rule, and the good news of His kingdom will be told in all the world
wrong: That God will give us our food today
That God will forgive us as we forgive others
That God will keep us away from evil
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: 'Told, believed, and obeyed everywhere' is catechism wording. The verses show God's kingdom and will coming on earth (Matthew 6:10) and the good news of the kingdom being preached in all the world (Matthew 24:14). They say nothing about it being believed and obeyed everywhere.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Does God know everything?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Yes, nothing is hidden from God
wrong: Yes, but only the big things
Yes, but not what I will choose
Yes, but not what will happen tomorrow

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What two special things did Jesus give His church to do?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Baptism and the Lord's Supper
wrong: Building an ark and a tall tower
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: No verses were given. The number of sacraments is a church teaching that churches do not agree on (some say seven), and no verse says it. The new question asks which signs Jesus gave, which the verses in q10 show (Matthew 28:19, 1 Corinthians 11:23-25).

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Who gave us baptism and the Lord's Supper?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: The Lord Jesus

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: At the Lord's Supper, why did Jesus say to eat the bread and drink the cup?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: To remember Him
wrong: To fill up on lots of food
To show who is the richest
To have a party just for ourselves
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: No verses were given, and 'to mark out His followers, and to comfort them and make them strong' is catechism wording. The new question uses what Jesus himself says in 1 Corinthians 11:24-25: 'do this in remembrance of Me.'

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What is used when someone is baptized?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Water
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The verses show that water is used (Acts 8:36-38). 'Washing' is not in them, and 1 Peter 3:21 says baptism is 'not the removal of dirt from the body,' so calling it washing could confuse a child.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Who should be baptized?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: People who believe in Jesus

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Can God do all things?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Yes, God can do all he wants.
wrong: No, some things are too hard for God.
Yes, God does whatever people ask.
No, God can only do easy things.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Does Jesus care for little children? What did He say when they were brought to Him?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Let the little children come to Me, and don't stop them!
wrong: Send the children away, because I am too busy!
Let the children wait until they are grown up!
The children must learn all the rules first!

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Paul says people who are baptized into Jesus should now live how?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: A new life, no longer slaves to sin
wrong: Keep on sinning so God's grace grows
Just the same way as before
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: Romans 6 does not talk about a promise made at baptism. It says those baptized into Christ should walk in newness of life and no longer be slaves to sin (verses 4 and 6). The new question follows that, and one wrong choice uses the idea Paul rejects in verses 1-2.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: At the Lord's Supper, what does the bread stand for?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Jesus' body, given for us
wrong: Jesus' blood, poured out for us
The manna God sent in the desert
The crops God sends each year

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: At the Lord's Supper, what does the cup stand for?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Jesus' blood, poured out to forgive sins
wrong: The water Jesus turned into wine
The rain God sends on the fields

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Who should eat and drink at the Lord's Supper?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: People who first look at their own hearts, believe in Jesus, and love one another
wrong: Anyone at all, without thinking about it first
Only people who are rich and important
Only people who are hungry that day
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The verses don't say "sorry for sin." They say each person must examine himself and judge himself rightly (1 Cor 11:28, 31). They also say to believe in Jesus and love one another (1 John 3:23). The new answer uses what the verses say.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: After Jesus died, did he stay in the tomb?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: No, he rose on the third day
wrong: No, he rose on the second day
No, he rose after a whole year

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Where is Jesus now?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: In heaven, speaking to God for us
wrong: In the tomb, still lying there

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Will Jesus come again?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Yes, in His glory with all the angels, to judge all the nations
wrong: No, he will never come back
Yes, but secretly, so no one sees
Yes, but only to visit one town
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: In John 12:48 it is Jesus' word that will judge on "the last day," and John 12:47 says "I have not come to judge the world," so "to judge the world" could confuse a child. Matt 25:31-32 says He will come in His glory with all the angels, and all the nations will be gathered before Him. The new answer uses those words.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Where do we learn how to love and obey God?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: In the Bible, God's Word
wrong: In the stars in the sky

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What happens to a person when they die?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: The body goes back to dust; the spirit goes back to God
wrong: They are born again as someone else on earth
The body and the spirit both stop forever
The body gets up and walks again right away

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Will the bodies of people who have died be raised to life again?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Yes, when the last trumpet sounds
wrong: No, their bodies will never live again
Yes, but only the bodies of kings

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What is hell?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: A place of punishment that never ends
wrong: A happy place with God forever
A punishment that lasts only a short time
Just the grave where everyone rests

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What will happen to people who are right with God?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: They will live forever with Jesus in His Father's house
wrong: They will be born again on earth
They must first go to a place to be cleaned
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The word "heaven" is not in these verses. Matt 25:46 says the righteous go into eternal life. John 14:2-3 says Jesus prepares a place in His Father's house so they may be where He is. The new answer stays with those words.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What is heaven?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: A place of joy where God's people will always be with the Lord
wrong: A dark, sad place where people are kept far from the Lord
A place where people are with the Lord for only a little while
A place where no one is ever glad
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: "Glorious" is not in the verses. They say "joy in Your presence," "eternal pleasures," and "we will always be with the Lord." Two wrong choices were also too close: 1 Thess 4 calls the dead "asleep" and has them waiting for the Lord to come, so a child could fairly pick "the dead sleep" or "a waiting place." Both are replaced with choices the verses clearly rule out.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Who were the very first people God made?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Adam and Eve

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What did God make Adam and Eve from?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Adam from dust, Eve from Adam's rib
wrong: Both of them from the dust
Adam from water, Eve from dust
Adam from dust, Eve from a flower

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: After God made Adam from the dust, what did God breathe into him?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: The breath of life
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: Genesis 2:7 says God breathed the breath of life into the man. It does not talk about 'souls that will never die', and it does not say this about Eve. The new question asks what the verse really says.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Do you have a soul as well as a body?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Yes. Jesus said people can hurt the body but cannot kill the soul.
wrong: No, I only have a body.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: Matthew 10:28 does show we have a soul and a body. But it also says God can destroy the soul, so 'a soul that will never die' goes beyond the verse. The new answer uses Jesus' own words.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: God made you. What else did God make?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Everything
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: 'What else' only makes sense straight after the question before it. On its own, a child cannot tell what 'else' means. Colossians 1:16 says all things were created, in heaven and on earth, seen and unseen, so the answer stays 'Everything'.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Our catechism says one way we can tell we have a soul is that we can think about what?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: God and the life to come
wrong: What we can see and hear
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: No Bible verses were given for this question, so nothing backs up the answer. It comes from a catechism, not from a verse. The new wording says the answer comes from the catechism, so it doesn't look like a Bible fact. Please add a verse that supports it, or drop the question.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: How did God make Adam and Eve at the start?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: In His own image, and very good
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The verses do not say 'holy and happy'. Genesis 1:27 and 1:31 say God made them in His own image and that all He made was very good. The answer now uses those words.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What is a covenant?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: A serious promise made between two sides, like Jacob and Laban
wrong: A song we sing to God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: In Deuteronomy 29, God Himself makes a covenant with His people, so 'two or more people agree' leaves God out. Also, the wrong choice 'A meal people share' could trick a child, because Jacob and Laban ate a meal when they made their covenant (Genesis 31:46).

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: In the book of Hosea, God says Adam broke something. What did Adam break?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: God's covenant
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The verses never use the names 'covenant of works' or 'covenant of grace'. Those names come from teaching about the Bible, not from these verses. Hosea 6:7 says only that Adam broke (transgressed) the covenant.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Which tree did God tell Adam he must not eat from?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: The tree of the knowledge of good and evil
wrong: The tallest tree by the river
The fig tree by the gate
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The verses do not say 'covenant of works' or 'obey God perfectly'. Genesis 2:16-17 gives one clear command: do not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What job did God give Adam in the Garden of Eden?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: To work the garden and take care of it
wrong: To catch fish in the river
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The verses never say God promised Adam life if he obeyed. They only warn that he would die if he ate (2:17). The new question uses something the verses do say: Adam's job in the garden (2:15).

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What did God warn would happen if Adam disobeyed?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: He would die.
wrong: He would get no more food.
He would have to live alone.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Did Adam obey God's command about the tree?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: No, he ate the fruit God told him not to eat.
wrong: Yes, he obeyed God in everything.
Yes, only Eve ate the fruit.
Yes, he never touched the fruit.
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The answer is right, since Adam ate the fruit (Genesis 3:6, 3:12, 3:17). But the name 'covenant of works' is not in these verses. The question now asks about God's command, which the verses do give.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Not doing what God asks is a sin. In Psalm 78, what did the people fail to keep?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: God's covenant
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: 'Want of conformity' is an old catechism phrase. It is not in the verses and is too hard for young children. Also, the wrong choice 'Doing what God says not to do' is a kind of sin too, which could confuse a child. The new question keeps the idea (not doing what God asks) and uses Psalm 78:10.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Why did God make you and everything else?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: For his glory

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What does it mean to transgress?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Doing what God says not to do
wrong: Doing what God says to do

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: When God gave Adam his rule to obey, did Adam act just for himself?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: No; he stood for all people after him
wrong: Yes; it was only about Adam
No; he stood only for Eve
No; he stood only for the angels

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What did Adam's sin bring to all people?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Sin and death came to everyone
wrong: It made people never need God
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The verses do not say 'sadness'. ROM 5:12 and 5:19 say sin and death came to all people and many were made sinners.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: In Psalm 51, David said when he first became sinful. When was it?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Even before he was born
wrong: When he told his first lie
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The name 'original sin' is not in the verses. PSA 51:5 says David was sinful from the time his mother conceived him, so the question now asks about that.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Jesus told Nicodemus about entering God's kingdom. Can anyone enter it without being born again?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: No; Jesus said we must be born again
wrong: Yes, if we try hard to be good
Yes, if they are a teacher like Nicodemus
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: In the verses Jesus speaks of entering God's kingdom and being born again, not of 'heaven' or 'a new heart'. 'This sinful heart' only made sense with the question before it.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Jesus told Nicodemus about a change of heart. What is it called?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Being born again

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: How can you give glory to God?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: By loving him and doing what he says
wrong: By knowing lots of big words

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Who can change a sinner's heart?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: The Holy Spirit

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Can anyone be saved by keeping God's law?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: No, no one can be saved that way
wrong: Yes, some very good people can

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Why can no one be saved by keeping God's law?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Because everyone has broken it
wrong: Because it was only for Adam
Because nobody ever heard of it

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Before time began, God gave us his grace in someone. Who was it?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Christ Jesus, God's Son
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: 2TI 1:9 says God gave us grace in Christ Jesus before time began. It does not say a plan was 'made with' Christ, so the question now follows the verse.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Christ is the go-between of a new covenant. Who is it for, so they can get God's promised gift that lasts forever?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Those God has called
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: HEB 9:15 says Christ is the go-between of a new covenant for 'those who are called', not 'chosen'. 'Stood for' was also not in the verse.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: God sent his Son, born under the law. Why did he do it?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: To set free those under the law and make them God's children
wrong: To give us a new law to keep by ourselves
Only to show us good manners
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The verses do not say Christ 'promised' anything, and 'keep God's law for us' goes beyond them. GAL 4:4-5 says God sent His Son, born under the law, to redeem those under the law so we could become His sons.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Did Jesus ever do even the smallest sin?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: No; he was holy, innocent and pure
wrong: Yes; once when the devil tempted him
Yes; small ones he was sorry for
Yes; when he was a little boy

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: How could God's Son suffer?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: He became a real man, like us
wrong: He became an angel in heaven
He only pretended to be a man

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What does it mean that Jesus made atonement for us?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Jesus suffered and died to pay for our sins
wrong: Jesus taught people how to be good
God decided sin was not bad after all
Jesus did miracles to show his power
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The answer fits ROM 3:25 and 2CO 5:21. But the wrong choice 'God chose to just forget about sin' sounds too much like 2CO 5:19's 'not counting men's trespasses', so a child could take it as right. It is replaced with a choice that is clearly wrong.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: In the covenant of grace (God's plan to save his people), what did God the Father promise to do?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Make the people Christ would die for right with him, and make them holy
wrong: Die on the cross for his people himself
Become a man and keep God's law for sinners
Be born as a baby in Bethlehem
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The answer is right (Romans 8:30, 33 say God justifies; 1 Peter 1:2 says his people are made holy), but 'Make right with him' has no 'who', so it is hard for a child to follow. The wording is now clearer.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Why should you give glory to God?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: He made me and takes care of me
wrong: So people will think I'm good

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What does sanctification mean?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: God making sinners holy in heart and in what they do
wrong: God forgiving sinners and calling them right
God taking sinners into his family as children
God choosing sinners before the world began

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: For whom did Jesus obey and suffer?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: For those the Father gave him
wrong: For the angels who never sinned
For the people of Israel only
For people who were good enough

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What kind of life did Jesus live on earth?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: A poor and hard life
wrong: A rich life full of honor
A life as a powerful ruler

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: How did Jesus die?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: On the cross, in pain and shame
wrong: By a sword, at a king's order
By stones thrown outside the city

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Who will be saved?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Only those who turn from sin, trust Jesus, and live holy lives
wrong: Everyone, even if they never turn from sin or trust Jesus
Only those who are baptized and go to church
Only children born into Christian families

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What does it mean to repent?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: To be sorry for sin, hate it, and stop doing it, because it does not please God
wrong: To feel bad and do lots of church rituals
To do good deeds to pay God back for sin
To tell all your sins in front of the church

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What does it mean to believe in Jesus?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: To trust Jesus alone to save you
wrong: To trust Jesus and the church to save you
To believe Jesus was only a great teacher
To trust your good deeds to save you

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Can you turn from sin and trust Jesus all by yourself?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: No; God must draw you and work in your heart
wrong: No; only your parents can do it for you
Yes; you can if you try really hard
Yes; you believe first, and then God helps
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The verses given say the Father must draw a person (John 6:44) and God works in us (Philippians 2:13). They do not name the Holy Spirit or say we can do nothing good at all. The question also said 'you' while the answers said 'I'. The answer now follows the verses and keeps the same person throughout.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: How can you get the Holy Spirit's help?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: By praying and asking God for him
wrong: By doing enough good deeds to earn it
By being very clever and wise
By waiting until you are grown up

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: About how long ago did Jesus die?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: About two thousand years ago

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Before Jesus came, how were people who loved God saved?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: By believing in a Saviour who would come
wrong: By being good enough on their own
By keeping all of Moses' laws
By being born into Abraham's family

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Before Jesus came, how did God's people show they trusted in the Saviour to come?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: By giving sacrifices on God's altar
wrong: By living all alone in the desert
By wearing special clothes every day
By joining armies to fight for Israel

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What did those sacrifices point to?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Jesus, the Lamb of God, who would die for sinners
wrong: The animals Noah kept safe on the ark
The good harvest God gave each year
The kings who would rule over Israel

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Christ has three offices, or jobs, as our Saviour. What are they?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Prophet, priest, and king
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The answer is right, but the wrong choice 'Moses, Aaron, and David' is the best-known prophet, priest and king, so it is really the right answer again under other names and could confuse a child. I swapped it for a choice that is clearly wrong.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: How is Jesus a priest for us?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: He gave himself for our sins and prays to God for us
wrong: He gives God a new gift every single day
He first says sorry to God for his own sins
He lives far away and cannot hear us

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: How is Jesus a king?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: He rules over us and keeps us safe
wrong: He rules over just one small town
He lets other people rule over him
He leaves us to fight on our own

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Jesus is our prophet, the one who teaches us about God. Why do you need him to teach you?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Because I can't know God's ways by myself
wrong: Because I never need any help
Because I can teach Jesus new things

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: There is only one God. How many persons is he?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Three persons

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Jesus is our priest, who takes away sin. Why do you need him as your priest?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Because I have done wrong things
wrong: Because I have never done anything wrong
Because I can take away my own sins

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Why do you need Jesus as your king?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Because I am weak and can't save myself
wrong: Because I am strong enough on my own
Because I never need anyone's help

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: How many commandments did God give on Mount Sinai?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Ten

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What did God write the Ten Commandments on?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Two tablets of stone
wrong: The bark of a big tree
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: No verses were given. 'Decalogue' is not in the BSB and is too hard a word for children. The new question comes from Deut 4:13 (given with q6): God wrote the Ten Commandments on two tablets of stone.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What do the first four commandments teach us?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: How we should love and honor God
wrong: How we should treat other people
How we should look after our pets
How we should keep our rooms tidy

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What do the last six commandments teach us?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: How we should treat other people
wrong: How we should pray each day
How we should keep the Sabbath
How we should sing to God

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Is God pleased with people who honor him and trust in his love?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Yes; the LORD is pleased with those who honor him and hope in his love
wrong: No; he is only pleased with people who are big and strong
No; he only likes people who give him money
No; he doesn't care what people do
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: In Prov 8:17 the one saying 'I love those who love me' is wisdom, not God, so 'he says' was wrong. Ps 147:11 says the LORD is pleased with those who fear Him and hope in His loving devotion. The question and answer now follow that verse.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Is God unhappy with people who do not love and obey him?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Yes; God is a fair judge who is angry about the wrong things people do
wrong: No; God doesn't mind when people do wrong
No; God is only upset with people who never heard of him
No; God never judges anyone at all
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: Ps 7:11 says God is a righteous judge who feels indignation each day, and the verses around it show his anger is at evil. 'Angry at wrong every day' is close, but it can sound like God is always angry. It now says plainly that he is angry about the wrong things people do.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Who are the three persons of God?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit
wrong: The Father, the Son, and the angel Gabriel
The Father, the Son, and Mary
The Father, the Son, and King David

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What does the first commandment teach us?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: To worship only God
wrong: To keep the Sabbath day holy
To honor our father and mother

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What does the third commandment teach us?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: To honor God's name, his word, and all he does
wrong: To honor our father and mother
To not make idols to bow down to
To rest on the seventh day

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: On which day of the week did Paul and the believers in Troas meet to break bread together?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: The first day of the week
wrong: The seventh day of the week
The fourth day of the week
The sixth day of the week
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: No verse given calls a day 'the Christian Sabbath' or says the Lord's day (Rev 1:10) is the first day. Also, Exod 20:10 calls the seventh day the Sabbath, so the wrong choice 'the seventh day' could seem right. The new question asks what Acts 20:7 plainly says.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: What wonderful thing happened at dawn on the first day of the week, after the Sabbath?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Jesus rose from the dead
wrong: God rested from making the world
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: Matt 28:1-7 shows Jesus rose on the first day of the week, but no verse given says that is why it is called the Lord's day. The new question asks what happened that day.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: Jesus told the woman at the well what God is. What did he say?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: God is Spirit
wrong: A big man who lives in heaven
An angel who rules the other angels
A power in nature that cannot think
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: John 4:24 says only 'God is Spirit.' The part 'has no body like ours' is not in the verses. It could also confuse a child, because the Son became a man with a body. The answer now keeps only what Jesus said.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: How should we spend the Sabbath, God's special day?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Praising God, hearing His word, and doing good
wrong: Staying far away from God's house and His word
Never helping anyone, even someone who needs it
Forgetting all about God and just having fun
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The verses show praising God (Psalm 92), hearing God's word in the synagogue on the Sabbath (Luke 4:16-19) and doing good on the Sabbath (Matthew 12:12). None of them talks about praying on the Sabbath, so 'praying' was added.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.question: The sixth commandment says, "You shall not murder." What does it teach us?
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.answer: Not to kill anyone
wrong: Not to take things that aren't ours
Not to want what other people have
To rest on God's special day
creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:catechis.fixed: The sixth commandment in Exodus 20:13 is 'You shall not murder.' 'Put away angry feelings' comes from Colossians 3:8 and from church teaching about the commandment. It is not what the commandment says.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: What are the very first words in the Bible?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth."
wrong: "And God said, 'Let there be light,' and there was light."
"And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters."
"Then God said, 'Let Us make man in Our image.'"

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: What kind of land was the wilderness God led Israel through?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: A huge, dry land with no water
wrong: A green land with flowing streams
A land of forests and ripe fruit
A small, quiet land with many springs

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: The people were thirsty in the desert and grumbled at Moses. How did God give them water?
God came down on a mountain in fire and smoke, with thunder, and spoke His words to the people. Which mountain was it?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.fixed: "Where did God speak to the people?" is too vague. God speaks in many places, and other verses say the LORD speaks 'from Zion', so 'Mount Zion' could look right too. The new wording ties the question to this story, where God came down on Mount Sinai in fire and smoke and spoke His words (EXO 19:18-20; 20:1).

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: What did God tell Joshua when he became the leader of the Israelites?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: The water stopped when the priests stepped in
wrong: A strong wind blew the water away

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: What happened to Rahab, who had helped the spies?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: She and her family were kept safe

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: After the city of Ai was won, on which mountain did Joshua build an altar to God?
After building the altar, what did Joshua do in front of all the people?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: He read them all of God's law
wrong: He gave each tribe its land
He marched them around a city
He built a big tent for God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: On the day the sun stood still, where did God help Joshua win the great battle?
After Joshua and the Israelites won Canaan, what did the land come to be called?
When Cain and Abel grew up, what very wrong thing did Cain do?
wrong: He took all of Abel's sheep

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: The twelve tribes of Israel were named after whom?
Where did the people of Israel set up the Tent of Meeting, God's special tent?
Before Joshua died, what did he tell the people to do?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: Fear the LORD and serve Him
wrong: Choose a king to rule them

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: What did the people promise Joshua?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: "We will serve the LORD our God and obey Him."
wrong: "We will serve Joshua and obey him."
"We will serve the gods of the people around us."

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: The Israelites promised Joshua they would serve only the Lord. After Joshua and all his people died, what did the next Israelites do?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: They turned away from the Lord and served false gods
wrong: They served only the Lord and never turned away
They went back to live in Egypt
They threw away every idol in the land
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.fixed: The people who made the promise were Joshua's generation. Judges 2:10-11 says the next generation served the Baals, so 'they did not keep their promise' doesn't fit the people who promised. The wrong choice 'they served the Lord all their lives' could even be true of them. The question now asks about the Israelites who came after.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: When Israel turned away from the Lord to serve idols, what happened to them?
wrong: They were sent far away to other lands
A great flood covered their land

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: The Bible tells about the very first people, from Adam to Noah's father. What was special about them?
wrong: They were all taken up to God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: What did Deborah do for the Israelites?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: She helped Barak and the Israelites win a big battle against Sisera's army
wrong: She helped Samson fight the Philistines
She led them across the Jordan River
She helped them beat the Midianites
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.fixed: The verses given never say 'Canaanites'. They name Sisera, Jabin's army commander, and Barak, who led the men. The answer now uses those names, so it stays just as specific.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: The angel of the Lord called one man "mighty man" and sent him to save Israel from the Midianites. Who was he?
What did Gideon do for the people?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: He won battles against the Midianites
wrong: He won battles against the Philistines
He won battles against the Egyptians

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: How many men did God use to help Gideon win his big battle?
When the Israelites did wrong again, who did God let rule over them for forty years?
Who began to set Israel free from the Philistines?
What was Samson famous for?
What did Samson once pick up and carry away from a city?
When the Philistines caught Samson, what did they do to him?
wrong: They sent him away to Egypt

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: Of all the people from Adam to Noah, who lived the longest?
In the days when the judges ruled, which woman from Moab came to Bethlehem with Naomi?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.fixed: 'Good woman' is not in the verses given. The question now asks what Ruth 1 does say: in the days of the judges, Ruth the Moabitess came to Bethlehem with Naomi.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: Which priest was also a judge of Israel for forty years?
Which mother brought her little boy to Eli at the house of the Lord?
What did Hannah name her little boy?
Where did Samuel grow up?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: In the house of the LORD
wrong: In a tent in the desert

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: While the boy Samuel was lying down in the house of the LORD, what happened?
wrong: A bright star shone in the sky
A bird brought him a message
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.fixed: 'What came to Samuel' is unclear and hard for a child to follow. The verses say that while Samuel was lying down in the house of the LORD, the LORD called him by name (3:3-6). The question now says this plainly.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: Eli told Samuel what to say if the LORD called again. When the LORD called, what did Samuel say?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.fixed: The first times the LORD called, Samuel said 'Here I am' (3:4-8). He only said 'Speak, for Your servant is listening' after Eli told him what to say (3:9-10). The question now says which time it means.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: Before the flood, in Noah's time, were the people good?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: Nearly all of them were very bad
wrong: Only a few of them were bad

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: When Samuel grew up, what did he do all his life?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: He was the judge of Israel
wrong: He was the king of Israel

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: He brought the people back to God
wrong: He built the temple in Jerusalem

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: At Mizpah, the Philistines came to fight Israel and Samuel prayed. What did the LORD do?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: He thundered and made the Philistines run away
wrong: He sent food from the sky
He gave them the Ten Commandments
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.fixed: In 8:6 Samuel also prayed, and God then let the people have a king, so the wrong choice 'A new king' could also be right. The question now names the time at Mizpah when the Philistines came to fight (7:9-11).

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: How long was Samuel the judge of Israel?
Where was Samuel's home while he was judge?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: To be like the other nations

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: Samuel was not happy when the people asked for a king. What did he do?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.fixed: The verses say Samuel was displeased (8:6), but they never say why. The answer guessed at his reason. The verses do say what he did next: he prayed to the LORD.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: When the people asked for a king, what did God tell Samuel to do?
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: Listen to them and give them a king
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.fixed: The answer is right (8:7, 8:22), but on its own the question does not say when this happened. It now names the time the people asked for a king.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: Which man walked with God, and then was gone, because God took him away?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.answer: Noah, his wife, his sons, and their wives

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.question: What did David do to keep his father's sheep safe?
